duration.note: whole seconds; the storyboard's total budget

beats.note: the timed storyboard; spans should tile the budget with no gap or overlap. `angle` is framing, `action` is what happens; they join with a comma into one clause, so write `action` as a phrase that can follow one ('steam rising from the bread'), not a predicate ('frames the baker'). `camera` is this shot's camera motion woven into a sentence (motion type + amplitude 'with small/large amplitude' + speed 'at slow/fast speed'), e.g. 'pushes in with small amplitude at slow speed toward the door'. `transition` is the cut phrase opening a later shot (default 'the camera cuts to'); the first shot is un-timed and takes no transition. Only the shot start is emitted, as `[Shot N] At MM:SS.mmm`. `cut` (default true) says whether the beat opens a `[Shot N]` of its own; set it false and the beat folds into the shot before it as a timed moment inside one continuous take, composed camera-first as `At MM:SS.mmm, the camera pushes in ... as she lifts the mug` — the camera must lead, since a move written behind its action was measured not to render at all. On a no-cut beat `angle` is where the move arrives, written `into a wider view`, not a framing to cut to. Reach for it when only the framing or the camera changes; a real cut needs new information. `lines` are the shot's dialogue (see the lines schema).

beats[].camera_path.note: Optional camera planner, used instead of beats[].camera while present. 2–12 ordered keyframes; time is a fraction of the beat (0–1), azimuth is an unwrapped orbit offset (-720 to 720 degrees, positive camera-right), elevation is -89 to 89 degrees, distance is 0.05–4 times the opening radius. First keyframe is {time:0,azimuth:0,elevation:0,distance:1}; last time is 1. Timing follows the beat when retimed. This is prompt guidance, not geometric conditioning. Motion mode requires a video path and a single full-generation beat; it uses Ref2VA with saved still anchors inactive. Auto loop closure anchors the final frame only for one frozen ±360° path returning to its opening elevation/radius, a first image and no references or conflicting last image. Subject boxes use normalized coordinates. Experiments are text recipes only. Null restores handwritten camera text.

beats[].lines.note: spoken/sung lines in a shot. `speakers` are stable author keys mapped to (S1),(S2)... by first vocal appearance across the whole prompt (two keys on one line make a group tag (S1,S2)); a key keeps its ID across shots. `text` is the VERBATIM words (only these and the language go inside <d>[Language] ...</d>). `describe` is the identifying phrase at first appearance (voice/age/on- or off-screen), `verb` is says/shouts/sings, `delivery` the manner. `voiceover: true` emits the fixed phrase 'says in an off-screen voiceover' plus the note that the on-screen character's lips stay shut; `possessive` picks the word in that note ("his", "her", "the baker's" — default "their"). A line that crosses a cut is written as two lines on adjacent beats: the outgoing half sets `continuity: "into"`, the incoming half `"from"`, and each emits <scenetrans> at the seam. `cutoff: true` marks speech the end of the video truncates. `placement: "open"` moves the line to the front of the shot, right after the framing clause and ahead of the action — a line has no timecode, so where its sentence sits is the only thing that says when it lands. Default "" keeps it last.

cues.note: audio events pinned to the ruler; `end` null is an instant hit, set it for a sustained bed. Composed as `At MM:SS.mmm, ...` / `From ... to ..., ...` sentences in `overall_soundscape`. TESTED AND IT DOES NOT TIME (2026-08-25): a cue at 00:03.500 produced the clip's quietest moment at 3.5s, while the slam it named landed at 6.1s — the same 6.1s an untimed mention produced. Naming a sound works; timing it does not. The official format times shots, not sounds, and a cue is our own extension. Write the sound into the beat it belongs to and accept that H3 places it.

style.note: the style contract: medium, texture, palette, era. Fixes the look so it does not drift between shots.

overview.note: optional one-line scene overview. In the base modes it continues the style's opening clause INSIDE [Shot 1]; only the full-reference document lifts style and overview above the marker. Write it as a lower-case clause ('a rain-soaked alley at dusk'), not a capitalised sentence.

camera.note: global camera/cutting style, woven into [Shot 1] as a fallback. Prefer per-shot `beats[].camera` — the format wants motion woven into each shot, never stacked as a trailing label.

audio.note: the DIEGETIC soundscape in prose: ambient, physical-action and non-verbal human sound (wind, footsteps, breathing). Merged with `cues` and emitted as `overall_soundscape`. Dialogue and score do NOT go here. H3 generates stereo in the same pass, so an empty track is wasted.

music.note: non-diegetic score only the audience hears, emitted as `non_diegetic_music`. Describe instrumentation, tempo, rhythm and dynamics — not mood words. Empty composes to `N/A`. Music a character can hear (radio, jukebox) is diegetic and belongs in the shot instead.

screen_text.note: literal on-screen text, reproduced exactly in double quotes. Stated in [Shot 1], since the list carries no shot of its own — for signage that appears in a later shot, write it into that beat's `action` in double quotes instead, which is what the format wants.

negatives.note: kept for the editor but NOT composed into the prompt: H3 has no negative input and the official format has no negative section, so naming unwanted things would only summon them. Leave empty in new prompts.

references.note: omni-reference files that DRIVE reference-to-video (ref2v): the kind's node slot is fed the file at `path` (a name in ComfyUI's input dir, from /reference/upload). The prompt renders as the six-section full-reference document. `role` becomes the file's own `<Picture N>`/`<Video N>`/`<Audio N>` subject_definitions line and `retention` its retention_analysis marker (see reference_vocabulary; empty uses the per-kind default) — but ONLY when the file stands on its own, as a keyframe, a source video or an audio track. A picture that merely shows a person, a place or a prop is named by a `subjects` entry instead and writes no line of its own. Setting any reference renders the segment as ref2v. Set `member` (a cast id) and `slot` (0-based index into that member's `references`) instead of `path` to LINK one of a member's identity files rather than copy it: `kind`/`path` then resolve from the member at compose time, so swapping their sheet updates every segment, while `role` and `retention` set here override the member's for this segment only. A linked row also puts that member on screen, so it needs no entry in `cast`. Leave `member` empty for an ordinary file reference.

subjects.note: the `<Subject N>` layer: what the target video CONTAINS, as opposed to which files it was given. H3 tracks subjects, so a person or a location is a subject and the pictures of them are only its sources. `role` is the prose after `<Subject N> is`; `noun` is the word the citation hangs on (person / setting / object / speaker) and may be empty; `sources` are `references[].path` values that define it — a visual one loses its own `<Picture N>` line, an audio one keeps its `<Audio N>` line and gains a `for <Subject N> (Sx)` back-link. A cast member on screen who has identity files becomes a subject automatically at compose time, so do NOT write one for them; set `member` (a cast id) with no `sources` to override just that member's `role`/`retention` for this segment. Write a plain entry (no `member`) only for something with no cast identity behind it. `label` is for the editor and is never composed.

ref_task.note: ref2v only: the summary's task types (see reference_vocabulary.task_types), joined with ' + '. Empty infers a sensible default.

ref_summary.note: ref2v only: the one-paragraph summary after the task-type prefix. Uses the <Tag N> labels; do not introduce new ones here.

first_frame.note: keyframe image name in ComfyUI's input dir (from /reference/upload). Setting it renders the segment as image-to-video (i2v): the frame is the geometry anchor the clip starts from. Cannot be combined with `references` (different node).

last_frame.note: optional end keyframe image name (input dir). Pairs with `first_frame`; the clip resolves toward it.

mentions.note: `@Name` in any prose field is a link to a project cast member, resolved at compose time to whatever label routes to them: their `<Subject N>` when they have identity files, `the <noun> (Sx)` when they only speak, `the <noun>` when they have neither. Write `@Mara` rather than a typed `<Subject 2>` — the number is positional, so it moves whenever the shot gains or loses a member, and a typed one does not move with it. Mentioning a member also puts them on screen, the same way attaching their identity file does. Matched whole and case-insensitively, longest name first, so a name may hold spaces. Honoured in: style, overview, camera, audio, music, ref_summary, beats[].angle/action/camera, beats[].lines[].describe/delivery, and the `role` on a subject or reference. NOT honoured in beats[].lines[].text or screen_text — a character saying another's name out loud, or a name painted on a sign, must stay a name.

cast.note: project cast member ids that appear in this segment but never speak — a location, a silent character. A member who speaks is named by a line's `speakers` instead. The member's appearance, voice and identity files are folded in at compose time, so editing the member updates every segment naming them. See /cast.

undescribed.note: cast ids present in this segment whose `appearance` must NOT be stated in the opening clause. Being on screen normally writes that appearance in, which is right for an establishing shot and wrong for a close one — a location's appearance is a paragraph of window walls and doorways, and stating it asks the camera to show them. Use it to keep a member's identity files without the prose. Ignored for a speaker, who is identified on their line instead.

guard_identities.note: default true. When two speakers share a shot, appends one sentence telling the model they are different people and must not merge or swap. Co-present identities are where H3 blends faces; set false only when the sentence reads as noise.

camera_vocabulary.note: motion type + amplitude + speed, written as natural English inside the shot. Amplitude and speed are stated only when they carry meaning; medium amplitude and normal speed are left unsaid.

continuity_phrases: continues uninterrupted into the next shot
carries over from the previous shot

operations.note: Returns installed filenames and catalog availability. Use adapters compatible with the video model.

{project, loras: [{name, strength_model, enabled}]}. Up to 8 unique files, finite weights -2..2. Video prepare/reshoot/batch/extend also accept a loras override; [] bypasses. Extends otherwise inherit the parent's recorded stack. Put trigger words in Style. Copy prepared.loras into extra_data.video_prompter.loras when submitting.
`projects` is the active names; `entries` adds a row per project on every shelf, with its shelf, dates and `lineage` (the version family a duplicate shares with its original).
{name, shelf: active|archived|trashed}. Archiving hides a finished project; trashing is a recoverable delete. Restoring is the same call asking for `active`.
{name, new_name?} — copies takes and stills, inherits the lineage, and defaults to the next `vN` name in the family.
the whole project: `sources` is the bin (one lineage each, with the segments that planned it), `timeline.clips` is the edit.
convenience getter for one source, its segments, and depth 0's prompt dict
body {prompt}; returns composed text and lint findings. Resolve every error finding before saving.
body {prompt, ops}; ops are fix / refit / ratio, so the frame grid and contiguity rules are not reimplemented by the caller.

body {project, source, note?}; the source carries its segments, each with a prompt. Optional source.video_loras is {mode: inherit|custom|off, loras: [...]}; custom replaces project defaults and off bypasses them. Send source_id on video prepare requests to resolve this setting; custom/off also override parent LoRAs on extends. Omit `origin` and any open editor live-updates. `note` says where the save came from ("Gemini: made it faster") and is shown against the revision this save files.

operations.step: write or rewrite a prompt with a language model
operations.note: body {instruction, prompt? | project+source(+segment?), scope?}. One operation for both ways in: a whole scene from a description, and a targeted tweak ("make this faster") on a prompt that already says something. `scope` is "all", a field name, a list of field names, or "beat:N" — the model is shown the whole document for context but is only asked for, and only allowed to change, the fields in scope. A tweak therefore cannot wander, and does not pay to regenerate the fields it was never about. An existing prompt is defended in the turn as finished work rather than a draft to improve. Fields outside the authored set (references, keyframes, canvas) are not in the shape the model can answer in and come through untouched. The draft is re-linted and handed back for repair up to twice. Naming `project` and `source` applies it and files a revision, so it is undoable rather than asked about.

whether a key is set, which model it names, and whether it came from the environment or the settings file (`settings_file` in the reply says where that is). `?probe=1` also lists the models the key can see. A 503 from /llm/draft means neither source has one.

newest first, each with its composed text. The server files a revision itself whenever a save changes a prompt, so a rewrite is always reversible and no caller has to remember to snapshot. Segments in the ordinary project reply carry only a `revision_count`; the revisions themselves are served here so every save does not ship them.

body {project, source, segment?, revision}; puts that past prompt back on one segment and files the current one, so undoing an undo is just another restore. Scoped to the segment — unlike `/project/restore`, which rolls back the whole bin.
body {project, source, at?}; a clip is one use of a source. `/source/add` already makes one, so this is for a second use.

body {project, clip, start, end} in *lineage* seconds — the clock `source_in`/`source_out` use, not the ruler. A mute is a decision about a moment of the footage, so trimming or moving the clip carries it. `/mute/edit` {project, mute, start?, end?} and `/mute/delete` {project, mute}. To silence a whole clip use `/clip/edit` instead.

operations.step: mute a clip, or hear a different take
operations.note: body {project, clip, audio:{muted?, take?, gain_db?, offset?}}. `take` names the take to *hear* — for a re-roll whose picture you rejected and whose sound you kept — and null gives the clip its own sound back. Picture and sound share the clip's trim, so nothing has to be re-aligned. Same route also does source_in / source_out / speed / label / enabled / pin.

operations.step: choose which take a source plays
operations.note: body {project, source, path}; `path` is one take id per generation, root first. Checked against each take's recorded parent and refused with 409 if the chain does not hold up. `/gallery/pick` does the same from a single take id.

operations.step: split shots into their own source
operations.note: body {project, source, beats, segment?, name?, clip?}; `beats` are 0-based positions in that segment's storyboard (the numbering `beat:N` uses). The picked shots become a new bin item that has rendered nothing, each keeping its own length laid end to end from zero, on a budget rounded to the whole second. Style, sound, cast, references and subjects come across whole — it is the same scene; `first_frame`/`last_frame` are dropped unless the pick still opens or closes where they pointed. A copy, not a move: the original keeps its shots. Use it when one generation is being asked to hold more cuts than it can, or when a shot deserves a whole generation to itself.
body {project, source, prompt?}; adds one generation to the end of a source's chain. Intent only — nothing renders here.

operations.step: reuse a character or location across sources
operations.note: body {project, member:{id?, name, kind, appearance, voice?, references?, notes?}}; omit `id` to mint one. `kind` is character / environment / prop / voice. Point a prompt at the member by putting its id in a line's `speakers` (they speak) or in the prompt's `cast` list (they do not). The appearance, voice and identity files are resolved in at compose time, so editing the member updates every segment naming it. GET /cast?project=NAME lists them; GET /cast/usage?project=NAME&member=ID says which segments would be stranded by a delete; POST /cast/delete removes one.

get an image/video/audio into ComfyUI's input dir so it can drive a render. Send JSON {url} to fetch an http(s) file server-side, or a multipart file part to upload bytes. Returns {filename}; put that on the segment prompt's `first_frame`/`last_frame` (i2v) or a `references[].path` (ref2v). Render mode is then chosen automatically: keyframe -> i2v, references -> ref2v, neither -> t2v; both is a mode.conflict error.

operations.step: parse composed prompt text into structured fields
operations.note: body {text, duration?}; returns {prompt, structured} so a frozen composed prompt can be restored into editable beats, style, soundscape and music.

operations.step: refine or upscale an existing take
operations.note: body {source, take_id?, width, height, seconds?, frames?, seed?, prompt_text?, enhancement_mode?: h3|seedvr2|seedvr2_faces|redetail|redetail_pixel, enhancement_resolution?: original|1080p, redetail_scale?, guide_strength?, guided_resample?, face_refine?}. Builds a standalone refinement workflow linked to the parent take.

## MiniMax H3

[MiniMax H3](https://www.minimax.io/blog/minimax-h3) is MiniMax's general-purpose, omni-modal generation model. It jointly understands text, image, video, and audio, and generates video with **native stereo audio**: voice, sound effects, and music are modeled jointly in a single forward pass, not layered on afterward. Output is up to 2K resolution, 24fps, and up to about 15 seconds.

## ComfyUI links
- [ComfyUI#15224](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI/pull/15224)
- [🤗 Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3)

## About this workflow

**Key inputs**

- **prompt**: describe the shots, camera moves, and the accompanying audio (dialogue, SFX, music) in one block
- **width / height**: set via Resolution Selector. H3's native canvas is a 768px short edge, capped at 768x1344 pixels, rounded to a multiple of 32
- **duration (seconds)**: converted to a valid frame `length` by the Math Expression node, snapping up to the model's 17-frame-per-block (17k+5) grid at 24fps
